short: The second Norman king of England, noted for his ruthless administrative efficiency.
full:
William Rufus, the third son of William the Conqueror, inherited the English throne in 1087 while his elder brother Robert Curthose received the Duchy of Normandy. His reign was characterised by heavy taxation and aggressive exploitation of church revenues, keeping bishoprics vacant to divert their income to the royal treasury. He successfully suppressed baronial rebellions and expanded Norman influence into Wales and Scotland.

His sudden death in August 1100, caused by a stray arrow while hunting in the New Forest, ended his reign without an heir. His younger brother Henry immediately seized the treasury at Winchester and the throne. William's ruthlessness alienated contemporary monastic chroniclers, but his military and financial administration consolidated the unstable kingdom his father had conquered.
